issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal and its concrete subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat). Problem statement UML and the provided template Main show Animal with a single attribute 'name' and the Main uses single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). In the solution repository, Animal declares an additional 'age' attribute and provides a constructor Animal(String name, int age) (and each concrete subclass in the solution calls super(name, age)), requiring two-argument constructors. This discrepancy leaves students unsure whether to implement single-argument constructors (String name) as implied by the UML and template Main, or two-argument constructors (String name, int age) as in the solution, and may cause compilation or integration confusion when comparing student code to the reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across artifacts. Two viable fixes: (A) If 'age' is intended to be part of the exercise, update the problem statement UML and the template Main to include the 'age' attribute and show/expect constructors with (String name, int age) for Animal and all concrete animals; update examples in Main to call new Seal("Clarabelle", 2) etc. (B) If 'age' is not intended, modify the solution to remove the 'age' attribute and change Animal and all concrete subclass constructors to single-argument form Animal(String name) and Seal(String name), Pig(String name), Goat(String name); update any references accordingly. Choose one option so UML, template, and solution consistently specify the same constructor parameter lists.
